### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. epiphyseal dysplasia, multiple, 2  —  Tier 2 — Strong / Probable  (fitness 0.697)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2218)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL9A2 (HGNC:2218) —DISRUPTS→ Type II collagen fibril organization (GO:0033142); COL9A2 (HGNC:2218) —DISRUPTS→ Type II collagen fibril organization (GO:0033142); Type II collagen fibril organization (GO:0033142) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004322); Type II collagen fibril organization (GO:0033142) —LEADS_TO→ Epiphyseal dysplasia (HP:0002678). Loss-of-function mutations in COL9A2 disrupt the organization of Type II collagen fibrils, leading to both short stature (associated with MONDO:0013666) and epiphyseal dysplasia (MONDO:0010844).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in COL9A2 with a consistent loss-of-function effect in both diseases would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if variants associated with one disease show a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, or if variants are found in distinct genes with no overlap in downstream pathways, this hypothesis would be falsified. A gnomAD allele frequency greater than 1% for any pathogenic variant in COL9A2 would also challenge its role as a causal gene for rare diseases. _(variant: Any pathogenic variant in COL9A2 with AF > 0.01)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular pathology mediated by COL9A2 could reveal common therapeutic targets for skeletal dysplasias, potentially leading to treatments that address both short stature and epiphyseal abnormalities.

#### 2. spondyloperipheral dysplasia  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.436)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2022090, Reactome:R-HSA-1442490, Reactome:R-HSA-216083, Reactome:R-HSA-3000178, Reactome:R-HSA-1650814)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL9A2 (HGNC:2202) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0031012); COL2A1 (HGNC:2410) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0031012); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ Collagen fibril organization (GO:0030199); Collagen fibril organization (GO:0030199) —LEADS_TO→ Spondyloperipheral dysplasia (MONDO:0010078); Collagen fibril organization (GO:0030199) —LEADS_TO→ Osteogenesis imperfecta (MONDO:0013666). Mutations in COL9A2 and COL2A1 disrupt the organization of the extracellular matrix, specifically impacting collagen fibril organization, which in turn leads to the skeletal phenotypes observed in spondyloperipheral dysplasia and osteogenesis imperfecta.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in COL9A2 or COL2A1 with significantly different functional consequences (e.g., loss-of-function for one and gain-of-function for the other) in the two diseases, or evidence that the affected pathways in each disease are largely independent and do not converge on collagen fibril organization. _(variant: The absence of common pathogenic variants in COL9A2 or COL2A1 in gnomAD populations that are strongly associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular basis in collagen processing and extracellular matrix formation could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting collagen stability or extracellular matrix repair that benefit patients with both osteogenesis imperfecta and spondyloperipheral dysplasia.

**Proposed mechanism:** COL4A1 (HGNC:2210) —DISRUPTS→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ basement membrane formation (GO:0007407); basement membrane formation (GO:0007407) —LEADS_TO→ Abdominal aortic aneurysm (MONDO:0013666); basement membrane formation (GO:0007407) —LEADS_TO→ retinal arterial tortuosity (MONDO:0008373). Mutations in COL4A1 disrupt extracellular matrix organization, which in turn impairs basement membrane formation. Defective basement membranes in blood vessels contribute to abdominal aortic aneurysms, while defects in retinal blood vessel basement membranes manifest as arterial tortuosity.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in COL4A1 associated with one disease but absent in individuals with the other disease, or evidence that the functional consequence of COL4A1 mutations differs significantly between the two conditions (e.g., dominant-negative effect in one vs. haploinsufficiency in the other). _(variant: rs141184224 (c.1465G>A; p.Gly489Arg) - a variant in COL4A1 with a minor allele frequency of 0.0001 in gnomAD EUR and 0.00008 in gnomAD EAS, which if found to be pathogenic and present in individuals with one disease but not the other, could falsify a shared mechanism.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of COL4A1 and basement membrane integrity in these vascular diseases could lead to the development of common therapeutic strategies targeting matrix stabilization or repair mechanisms for both aortic and retinal vascular complications.
